sovereign_country.strategic_role: 北美成熟市场、联邦与省两级公司实体设立（EPC合规）

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Retail Sale via Internet - Marketplace FBA Store

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Federal Jurisdiction, Canada (Corporations Canada / Director under the Canada Business Corporations Act)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid — Common Law at the federal level, with Quebec civil law preserved; federal corporate law applies uniformly
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Canada–European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA)
Canada–China Foreign Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (2014)
Convention Between Canada and the United States of America with Respect to Taxes on Income and on Capital (1980)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c 17, as amended; Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46, s 462.3 et seq.; Canada Business Corporations Act, RSC 1985, c C-44, ss 21.1–21.7 (individuals with significant control register) and related regulations; Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c 17; Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, SC 2011, c 21; FINTRAC Guidance 2, 4, 7 and Transaction Reporting Regulations; Canada’s Convention with respect to Apostille in force since 11 January 2024.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copy of each director and significant shareholder / UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport issuing authority (e.g., Public Security Bureau for Chinese nationals; Passport Office for other countries)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if country of issuance is party to the Apostille Convention; otherwise Consular Legalization at the Canadian embassy/consulate in the country of issuance

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized proof of residential address (bank statement or utility invoice) for each director and UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing bank or utility provider, duly notarized by a local notary public

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of no criminal record / police clearance certificate for each director and UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National or provincial police authority in the country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter confirming source of funds and account conduct
Certificate of incumbency / certificate of good standing from any corporate shareholder entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registered agent or corporate registry in the shareholder’s jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney authorizing the Canadian incorporation agent and counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public authorized by the principal

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, officers, shareholders and UBOs against the Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List, United Nations Security Council sanctions lists, OFAC SDN list, INTERPOL Red Notice database, and Canada’s domestic administrative sanctions. PEP identification follows FINTRAC definitions; enhanced due diligence applies to foreign political exposure, family members, known associates, and source-of-wealth anomalies. Attorneys and corporate service providers must verify identity and maintain records under PCMLTFA record-keeping and reporting obligations, including any suspicious transaction reporting to FINTRAC.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Corporations Canada Online Filing Centre — NUANS Name Search Request via Corporations Canada or an authorized NUANS service provider
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A CBCA corporate name must contain a distinctive element, a descriptive element, and a legal element. The name may be in English, French, or a bilingual equivalent. If a non-official language script is used, the name must also provide a romanized transliteration in the NUANS report so that the distinctive element is searchable in the Canadian marketplace. The legal element must appear in one of the official languages or an acceptable abbreviation (e.g., Inc., Corp., Ltd., Limitée, Inc.). Names must not be misleading as to business activity or affiliation.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: No extension is available for a name reservation; after 90 days, a new NUANS search is required. On rejection, the applicant may submit a written reconsideration request to the Director of Corporations (Corporations Canada) within 30 days of the refusal notice. The request must include a fresh or existing NUANS report, legal arguments distinguishing the rejected name from cited conflicting names, evidence of consent from the owner of a conflicting trademark or business name if any, and any proposed amendment to the distinctive element. If the Director upholds the rejection, the applicant may seek judicial review before the Federal Court of Canada within 30 days of the reconsideration decision.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for a low-risk marketplace FBA store where the corporation maintains a physical Canadian street address through a registered agent located in the province of the registered office; the registered address must be an actual location capable of receiving service of process, not merely a post office box. A non-resident corporation may use a law firm or corporate services provider’s address for service. For GST/HST purposes, CRA also accepts the Canadian registered agent address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low; annual risk of unannounced physical inspection is approximately 2–5% for a low-risk online marketplace retailer, with inspections triggered only by returned mail, inconsistent tax filings, complaints, or random administrative sample audits.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office / registered agent service — first year

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for Canadian federal registered agent service

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Certified notary public in country of origin and Canadian embassy/consulate or Apostille authority
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market rate for notarial and authentication package

Pre-incorporation legal opinion on non-resident ownership and CBCA compliance

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Hourly advisory benchmark with fixed-scope estimate

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Canada Business Corporations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44 (CBCA), particularly s. 5(1) (incorporation), s. 8 (articles of incorporation), s. 12 (certificate of incorporation), s. 16(1) (corporate powers), s. 106 (board of directors) and s. 115 (first directors); Canada Business Corporations Regulations, 2001, SOR/2001-512.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED), Online Filing Centre
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form 1) under the Canada Business Corporations Act
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is required under the CBCA. The corporation may issue one or more shares with or without par value, and no escrow account, capital deposit, or paid-up capital minimum is imposed. Consideration for issued shares may be satisfied in money, property, or past service under CBCA s. 25(1). Non-resident ownership is permitted.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) The Corporation subscribes for and accepts all issued shares described in the Articles of Incorporation and records paid-up capital in accordance with the Canada Business Corporations Act. (2) The registered office shall be and remain at the address filed with Corporations Canada until changed by board resolution. (3) The following officers are appointed: Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer, and Corporate Secretary, each with standard executive functions, signing powers, and duties imposed by the by-laws; (4) Officers are directed to register the Corporation with taxation authorities, open the Corporation’s bank accounts, execute operational contracts, and take all necessary industrial and municipal licensing steps.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Search and Reservation through NUANS
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada Name Reservation / NUANS Online Services, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS-based name search for the proposed corporate name to ensure distinctiveness. File a name reservation request, which remains valid for up to 90 days. Attach the NUANS report or reservation confirmation to the Articles of Incorporation at filing time. If the name contains regulated or distinctive terms, include the necessary consent letters.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name with distinctive element
NUANS search report or name reservation confirmation
Consent letters for regulated or distinctive terms, if applicable
Declaration of permissible corporate name usage
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for being confusingly similar to an existing name, submit a formal re-examination request to Corporations Canada within 30 days or amend the Articles with a new distinctive name and re-file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Submit Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form 1 under CBCA s. 8, specifying the authorized share structure and share class rights, number of directors, first registered office city, and first directors. Submit the form electronically through Corporations Canada's Online Filing Centre, attach the NUANS report and director consents, and pay the prescribed filing fee.
required_dossiers: Form 1 (Articles of Incorporation)
NUANS report or name reservation certificate
Director consent forms
Notice of registered office, if used as ancillary filing
Filing fee payment confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Corporations Canada issues a request for correction due to incomplete or defective articles, correct and resubmit the Articles within the stated correction window to avoid deemed withdrawal; no additional fee is required if the correction is submitted on time.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receipt of Certificate of Incorporation and Corporate Existence
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After substantive review of the Articles, the Director General issues a Certificate of Incorporation under CBCA s. 12. The corporation comes into existence on the date stated in the certificate. Download and retain the certified certificate, filed Articles, and accompanying corporate records, and issue any initial share certificates.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation issued by Corporations Canada
Filed Articles of Incorporation
Registered office address and list of first directors
Corporate by-laws and minute book records
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is rejected or delayed because of unsatisfactory corrections, promptly resubmit the corrected Articles if the correction window is still open; otherwise a new application, refiling fee, and re-executed dossiers will be required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Meeting, Share Subscription, and Officer Appointments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: First Board of Directors (internal corporate governance; CBCA Part VII)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold a meeting of the first board of directors. Pass the first board resolution approving the issuance of subscribed shares, adopting the registered office address, appointing the Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer, and Corporate Secretary, adopting by-laws, and authorizing opening of bank accounts and execution of operational contracts.
required_dossiers: Notice of first board meeting or resolution in lieu of meeting
Certificate of Incorporation and Articles of Incorporation
Director consents and conflict-of-interest declarations
Share subscription agreements and payment records
By-laws and corporate registers for directors, officers, and shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a proposed director or officer refuses to act, replace the individual by written resolution before share issuance; ensure that all resolutions are signed by unanimous consent where permitted and filed in the corporate minute book.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal Business Number and Provincial Extra-Provincial Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency Business Registration Online; applicable provincial corporate registries (e.g., Ontario, British Columbia, Quebec)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the federal corporation with the Canada Revenue Agency through Business Registration Online to obtain a Business Number and program accounts (GST/HST, payroll, import/export, if applicable). If the corporation maintains physical premises in a province other than its jurisdiction of formation, file an extra-provincial registration in each such province.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Registered office address
Directors' and officers' legal names and addresses
Description of business activities (ISIC 4791 / NAICS 454110)
Provincial extra-provincial registration form where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CRA Business Registration application is rejected due to corporate name or office mismatch, correct the underlying information with Corporations Canada and resubmit; provincial extra-provincial registration may require a certified federal certificate, and if requested, an apostille or legalization.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — no federal or provincial industrial licensing board administers an operating permit for ISIC 4791 (retail sale via internet). For physical premises, the competent authority is the municipal business licensing office in the operating city (e.g., Municipal Licensing and Standards Division).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — no statutory operating or manufacturing license is mandated for a non-manufacturing e-commerce retail marketplace activity. A general municipal business license and occupancy certificate may be required where an office or fulfillment space is leased.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC); provincial counterpart environmental ministry where applicable
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not designated — activity does not constitute a designated project under the Impact Assessment Act, S.C. 2019, c. 28, s. 11, and does not require a federal environmental impact assessment. No EIA registration is required for warehouse/office operations incidental to e-commerce retail; municipal zoning, wastewater, and waste by-laws still apply.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial effluent discharge is generated; any wastewater discharge must comply with municipal sewer-use by-laws. If refrigeration or vehicle fleets are used, the corporation must comply with CEPA 1999 ozone-depleting substances and HFC regulations, applicable VOC reporting thresholds, and provincial packaging and extended producer responsibility obligations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification under the National Fire Code and provincial fire codes; occupancy clearance under the National Building Code; and occupational health and safety compliance under Canada Labour Code Part II for all physical workplaces. No specialized structural load inspection is required unless racking, mezzanines, or other modifications exceed the applicable building permit threshold; WHMIS training is required for staff handling cleaning or hazardous materials.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC) – official portal: My Business Account (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html); Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) administers import/export fiscal controls via the CARM portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A federally or provincially incorporated Business Corporation obtains its 9-digit Canadian Business Number (BN) through CRA after incorporation (Corporations Canada or provincial registry). Program accounts: RC for GST/HST and RM for corporate income tax. Non-resident corporations carrying on business in Canada must register for GST/HST within one month of exceeding CAD 30,000 in taxable Canadian supplies in the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters; the non-resident simplified registration is available via Form RC4592 or online through CRA's Non-Resident Registration desk. For Amazon FBA marketplace-facilitated sales, Amazon is the deemed GST/HST supplier effective 1 July 2021 and collects/remits tax; the seller remains liable for corporate income tax registration and must file Form RC1 to obtain the BN if no other program account exists. Voluntary registration is permitted below threshold only if a taxable supply is being made in Canada.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box flow-through election exists for a Canadian Business Corporation. Domestic elections include: section 85 rollover election (tax-deferred property transfer to a corporation); section 83(2) capital dividend election; section 249.1 non-calendar-year fiscal period election; Capital Cost Allowance class elections; and section 150(2) treaty election for foreign affiliates. Hybrid mismatch rules (Income Tax Act ss. 12.8, 18.7, 20.2, 94A) apply to payments made after 1 December 2023 and contain ordering and adjustment rules rather than elective opt-out mechanisms.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 of taxable supplies made in Canada in the immediately preceding four calendar quarters and the current quarter (federal small-supplier threshold); non-resident suppliers using the simplified digital/e-commerce GST/HST regime apply the same CAD 30,000 specified threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not mandate real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction controls, API pre-clearance, or digital stamping. E-invoicing is voluntary under the Canada E-Invoicing Interoperability Framework (Peppol BIS 3.0). Registrants must retain electronic books and records in a coherent machine-readable format (Excise Tax Act, section 286) for six years; export zero-rating evidence must be retained as required to substantiate claims upon CRA audit.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rated status applies to tangible personal property physically exported by the supplier (Excise Tax Act, Schedule VI, Part V, section 20) and to services supplied to a non-resident meeting the exported-service criteria (Schedule VI, Part V, section 7) when the service is not enjoyed in Canada. The supplier must export the goods as soon as reasonable after delivery and before tax becomes payable, and must retain contemporaneous evidence of physical export, foreign payment, and commercial terms to support the 0% rate and associated input tax credit/refund claims.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (CBSA ACI eManifest via Canadian Export Declaration or CARM portal)
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / Cargo Control Document evidencing physical export from Canada
Commercial invoice and purchase order specifying exporter, buyer, HS classification, value, and destination country
Inward Remittance Certificate (foreign exchange proof of payment from the non-resident purchaser for offshore services or intangible supplies)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may reassess zero-rated supplies within the four-year normal reassessment period, or without time limit in cases of misrepresentation or fraud, clawing back uncollected GST/HST plus compounding daily arrears interest. Civil penalties include Excise Tax Act section 285 false-statement penalties (25% of the misstated net tax), section 280.1 failure-to-file penalties, and Income Tax Act section 163(2) gross negligence penalties (50% of understated corporate income tax). Fraudulent export zero-rating also exposes the seller to CBSA seizure, forfeiture, loss of export privileges, and criminal prosecution under the Customs Act and Criminal Code.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains a floating exchange rate regime with full convertibility for current account transactions. Capital account transactions are subject to Bank of Canada review and approval for certain thresholds and investor types. Profit remittances from Canadian corporations are permitted without restriction when tied to operational business activities.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender of export proceeds to the Bank of Canada. Foreign exchange transactions must be reported to FINTRAC for AML compliance. For cross-border e-commerce sales, proceeds are received in foreign currency and converted at market rates through licensed banks.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High viability for fintech EMI providers including Stripe, Airwallex, and Wise for cross-border e-commerce. Legal constraints require FINTRAC registration and full AML/KYC compliance for all cross-border transfers.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote KYC and onboarding is fully permitted for Canadian corporations. Directors must provide corporate documents, beneficial ownership information, and source-of-funds verification; physical appearance is not required except for high-value or enhanced due diligence cases.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions screening adverse match or Politically Exposed Person identification
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporate resolution authorizing account, beneficial ownership certificate, detailed source of wealth and funds documentation, and legal opinion confirming compliance

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistent transaction patterns or links to high-risk jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business plan, audited financial statements, third-party verification reports, and transaction history demonstrating legitimate commercial activity

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital injections via SWIFT MT103 wire transfers with purpose codes including 'Capital Contribution', 'Equity Injection', or 'Share Capital'. All transactions require corporate board resolution and verified beneficial ownership documentation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for trade settlements primarily via SWIFT MT103 for international payments. Commercial Letters of Credit are available through partner banks for specific trade transactions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CBCA Annual Return (Corporations Canada online annual return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each anniversary date of the certificate of incorporation; not a fixed calendar date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Two consecutive missed annual returns allow Corporations Canada to issue a notice of intended dissolution; after 120 days, a certificate of federal dissolution may be issued without further notification. Reinstatement requires an application, a missing-file compliance filing, and payment of any applicable reinstatement fee.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (including financial statements required by the CRA if prepared)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the fiscal year-end; e.g., a December 31 fiscal year-end is due June 30 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty under Income Tax Act s.162(1): 5% of the balance of unpaid tax, plus 1% per full month of default to a maximum of 12 months. CRA will also charge daily compound interest under s.161; continued default may lead to a gross-negligence penalty, an arbitrary assessment, and director liability for unremitted source withholdings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GST/HST Annual Return (for an annual filing electric-retail registrant under the normal CRA GST/HST threshold)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual GST/HST filers must file no later than three months after the GST/HST fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Under the Excise Tax Act, a failure-to-file penalty of 6% of the net tax returnable plus 1% per month late (maximum 12 months); interest accrues at prescribed rates, and an assessed return may be issued by CRA.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the CBCA, every corporation must appoint a licenced public accountant as auditor unless the corporation is not a distributing corporation and all shareholders unanimously consent in writing to dispense with the auditor. There is no revenue or asset threshold in the CBCA; the unanimous-consent waiver must be renewed for each financial year and kept in the minute book.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: For distributing/reporting issuers: IFRS as incorporated in the CPA Canada Handbook. For non-distributing CBCA private corporations: ASPE is generally applied, although IFRS may be elected. Financial statements must present fairly and include comparative prior-year figures in accordance with Canadian GAAP.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: At each annual general meeting, the corporation must review the Register of Individuals with Significant Control ('ISC') and update it within 15 days after any change in significant control. All share transfers, issuances, or voting/board-control changes that cause an individual to hold, directly or indirectly, 25% or more of a class of shares or 25% of votes, or to control the corporation through agreements, must be recorded. The ISC register is not filed with Corporations Canada as a separate statutorily required annual filing; it remains at the registered records office, subject to CRA and shareholder inspection, and must be made available to Corporations Canada on request.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500–12,000 for a non-distributing private retail e-commerce corporation

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Federal General Rate Reduction yields 15% headline; Small Business Deduction (for Canadian-controlled private corporations) can reduce the federal rate to 9% on up to CA$500,000 of active business income per year; SR&ED investment tax credits and accelerated Capital Cost Allowance are available for qualifying expenditures.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return; filed electronically through the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) EFILE system or approved third-party software (mandatory for most corporations).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 6 months after the fiscal year-end date (e.g., a December 31 year-end must be filed by June 30 of the following year). Balance-due day on unpaid taxes generally falls 2 months after year-end for CCPCs and 3 months for non-CCPCs.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income (loss) before adjustments; reconciles financial statement income with tax reporting, including FBA sales, COGS, and operating expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only Canadian-source business income attributable to carrying on business in Canada; foreign e-commerce income unrelated to a Canadian permanent establishment need not be included.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income (loss) after deducting adjustments, interprovincial income allocation, and loss carryovers; this is the base for federal and provincial tax calculation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents with a Canadian permanent establishment must allocate taxable income in accordance with the OECD model and Canada's provincial allocation rules; treaty protection must be asserted properly.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal tax computed at the applicable corporate rate on taxable income before credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply treaty credits and foreign tax credits if applicable; the non-resident entity remains liable for federal tax on Canadian-source PE income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Information return covering dividends, interest, rents, and royalties paid to non-resident related parties, triggering Part XIII withholding obligations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose all payments to non-arm's length non-residents; any unreported distribution or notional dividend may be reassessed as deemed payment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late-filing penalty is 5% of the balance owing plus 1% per month up to 12 months (maximum 17%); additional penalties apply for repeated failure, gross negligence, and failure to file information returns (e.g., T106) with per-transaction penalties up to CA$25,000.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim treaty-reduced withholding on dividends, the non-resident beneficial owner must provide a completed CRA residence certification form (NR301/NR302 series) and, if requested, an official Certificate of Residence from the home tax authority (e.g., U.S. IRS Form 6166). Submission must be made to the Canadian payer before payment; retroactive refund claims may be made to the CRA through the T2/Part XIII process.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Part XIII withholding rate is 25% on royalties and interest paid to non-residents; under the Canada-U.S. Tax Treaty, interest is generally exempt (0%) when the beneficial owner is a U.S. resident dealing at arm's length, and royalties for copyright, patents, and trademarks are generally subject to 10% withholding.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not maintain a separate Economic Substance Regulation (ESR) framework (as in offshore financial centres) but applies the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) under s.245 to disregard arrangements lacking genuine economic substance. Additionally, CRA may re-characterize transactions under transfer pricing rules and rely on treaty abuse denials in cross-border situations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willfully omitting or falsely reporting Amazon FBA sales revenue, creating fictitious expenses, or hiding offshore accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal prosecution under Income Tax Act s.239(1): on indictment, fine of up to 200% of tax evaded and imprisonment up to 5 years; civil reassessment and gross negligence penalties of 50% of understated tax are also applicable.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who participate in or authorize evasion may be jointly and severally liable for the resulting tax and penalties; criminal exposure can lead to travel bans, extradition procedures, and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a Canadian corporation solely to strip profits through management fees or intercompany charges without real employees, physical premises, or substantive business decision-making.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA reassessment under GAAR (s.245) denying the tax benefit and imposing interest and penalizing adjustments; possible transfer pricing re-characterization under s.247.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable as promoters or planners of the avoidance arrangement; penalties include civil restitution, future compliance obligations, and in file-closure cases, criminal sanctions for culpable conduct.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting FBA service fees, supply chain markups, or royalty payments to a foreign related party at rates inconsistent with non-arm's length pricing, causing profit shifting out of Canada.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Income Tax Act s.247(2)(3) transfer pricing adjustments, secondary adjustments, and administrative penalties equal to 10% of the net transfer pricing adjustment where the aggregate value of transactions exceeds CA$5,000,000 in the year.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who knowingly sign false transfer pricing documentation can be liable as participants in a false statement for tax purposes; penalties may include fines and imprisonment under s.239(1).

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to Remit Part XIII Withholding Tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, royalties, or cross-border management fees to a foreign parent or shareholder without calculating and withholding the statutory 25% (or applicable treaty-reduced) Part XIII tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Unpaid withholdings being assessed as a debt owed to the Crown, plus interest and penalties; CRA may reassess the payer as the agent of the non-resident and collect the amounts due.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for unremitted withholding taxes under Income Tax Act s.227.1 if they were in control at the time the obligation arose, without benefit of the due diligence defence.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using layered shell corporations, nominee directors, and offshore intermediary accounts to conceal the true beneficial ownership of the FBA business while failing to report to FINTRAC as a money services business or carrying on prohibited cross-border transfers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, failure to comply can result in administrative monetary penalties up to CA$500,000 for a corporation and imprisonment for individuals; Criminal Code laundering offences carry sentences up to 10 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who authorize or fail to prevent laundering activities may be criminally liable and personally subject to asset seizure, civil forfeiture, travel prohibition, and conviction-based imprisonment.
